ai.description: This slender, worm-like snake reaches 20–25 cm. It is uniform dark brown or purplish-black with a pale snout and tail tip. Key features include a blunt head, tiny eyes, and 14 midbody scale rows.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Gerrhopilus beddomii* is best distinguished by its lack of a preocular scale, as the prefrontal and ocular scales meet to border the eye directly.
ai.habitat: *Gerrhopilus beddomii* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 500 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Beddome's worm snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending its time burrowing through moist soil and leaf litter in search of small invertebrates like termites.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gerrhopilus beddomii* is oviparous, laying small clutches of elongated eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: Gerrhopilus beddomii is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 600 and 1,500 meters.
